We expand the parentheses using the **distributive property**:

$\blueD A(B+C)=\blueD A\cdot B+\blueD A\cdot C$

We can also think about the problem using an area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Two rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of w squared and a length of negative four w. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative nine with a length of negative four w.

hints.content:
Here's how the solution goes, algebraically:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\goldE{-4w}(w^2-9)
\\\\
&=\goldE{-4w}(w^2)+(\goldE{-4w})(-9)
\\\\
&=-4w^3+36w
\end{align}$

Here's how the solution looks in terms of the area model:

Inside of this rectangle is negative four w cubed. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative nine with a length of negative four w. Inside of this rectangle is thirty six w.
